document.description: lspA encodes type II signal peptidase (SPase II, lipoprotein signal peptidase) of Bacillus subtilis, a polytopic cytoplasmic-membrane aspartic protease of the peptidase A8 family that removes the signal peptide from diacylglyceryl-modified prolipoproteins immediately upstream of the lipidated lipobox cysteine, the second step of lipoprotein maturation after Lgt. Asp-102 and Asp-129 are the proposed catalytic residues. The B. subtilis enzyme complements an E. coli lsp mutant, but unlike its E. coli counterpart it is not essential for viability; lspA-null cells grow, although they are impaired at low and high temperatures, accumulate lipid-modified PrsA precursor and secrete alpha-amylase poorly. B. subtilis has no recognized Lnt ortholog, so its lipoproteins are not N-acylated by the diderm route.

description: lspA encodes type II signal peptidase (SPase II, lipoprotein signal peptidase) of Bacillus
  subtilis, a polytopic cytoplasmic-membrane aspartic protease of the peptidase A8 family that removes
  the signal peptide from diacylglyceryl-modified prolipoproteins immediately upstream of the lipidated
  lipobox cysteine, the second step of lipoprotein maturation after Lgt. Asp-102 and Asp-129 are the proposed
  catalytic residues. The B. subtilis enzyme complements an E. coli lsp mutant, but unlike its E. coli
  counterpart it is not essential for viability; lspA-null cells grow, although they are impaired at low
  and high temperatures, accumulate lipid-modified PrsA precursor and secrete alpha-amylase poorly. B.
  subtilis has no recognized Lnt ortholog, so its lipoproteins are not N-acylated by the diderm route.
